note_en: 把 moves the object in front of the verb: 不要把身份证号、密码这些信息告诉陌生人 "don't tell strangers information like your ID number and password." English keeps the object after the verb, but Chinese often uses 把 when the sentence focuses on what happens to a specific thing, especially with verbs like 告诉, 加入 and 给 that also take a second object. The same pattern appears in 把网络安全知识加入了课程 "added cybersecurity to the curriculum."
